html:
SMTO-GML-0050 — Your saved Gmail account details are incomplete or invalid

GUID: c95d6ad2-d740-5f16-870a-b8c1b875c6c3
Slug: gmail-app-password-setup
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • SMTO checked the Gmail account saved in Parameter Store and found a problem, such as a missing app password, an unusable email address, or mail set to come from a different address. This step stopped before sending anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options (the three dots at the top of SMTO) › Parameter Store and select your Gmail account. If there is none, pick the Gmail — App Password (Gmail + SMTP) template and select New. SMTO reads the Gmail address and app password only from this saved entry.
  2. Open the Value tab and select Reveal & edit value. Make sure email is your full Gmail address, app_password is the app password from Google, and timeout_seconds is between 1 and 120. Select Save. SMTO refuses the entry if a value is missing, the address is malformed, the password has unusual characters, or the timeout is out of range.
  3. Make sure your request sends mail from the same address that is saved in this entry, and that it mentions this app-password account with @. SMTO only drafts, sends and tests the connection for the address and account type saved here.
  4. Before asking again, open Gmail and check Sent and Drafts for anything this request already created, then ask SMTO only for what is missing. Earlier steps of the same request may have finished, and repeating them could create duplicates.

What success looks like

  • Asking SMTO to test the Gmail connection succeeds, and your request completes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Never paste your app password into a conversation, and don't switch to a different account or sign-in method to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected gmail_app_password_account parameter failed validation, the outgoing message's From address did not match the saved Gmail address, or a connection test targeted an account that is not an app-password account.

What this means

  • The saved profile or fixed sender does not meet the Gmail app-password contract. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: The saved profile or fixed sender does not meet the Gmail app-password contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • Correct or recreate the parameter from the 'Gmail — App Password (Gmail + SMTP)' template: profile_type gmail_app_password_account, profile_version 1, a valid email, a printable-ASCII app_password (1–256 characters) created with Google 2-Step Verification, integer timeout_seconds 1–120, and no extra keys. Ensure the outgoing MIME From equals the saved email (gmail_sender_invalid) and that gmail.test_connection targets an app-password account (gmail_app_password_account_required).
  • Open the Gmail — App Password (Gmail + SMTP) template in Parameter Store. Enter the Gmail address and an app password created with Google 2-Step Verification, then save and select that reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
  • App-password setup: https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
